label: GO step late in the episode (trial >= ~89) after a rewarded trial
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (99.6% of mass), never at D2, and only in the last ~12 trials of the 100-trial episode (zero activity before trial 80; 96% of mass in trials 90-99). It acts like an end-of-episode clock, and it matches the value head falling (99% of mass where value < 5.22). Within that late range it is much stronger after a rewarded previous trial: activation ramps up over consecutive rewarded GO steps, and an unrewarded trial drops it to near zero or silences it. It is more frequent on a2 choices / when S2 is good (about 70% of mass), and the highest activations come at the final trials (~99). Only observed variables are used (ep_trial is elapsed time, prev_reward is the D1 input). An alternative, (phase==GO)&(value<5.22), has F1 0.77 with recall 0.94. Adding an extra clause for ep_trial>=95 regardless of reward gives F1 0.82, which I judged not worth the added complexity. Misses are mostly weak activations at trials 85-88, or after an unrewarded trial very near the end.

issues: Every factual claim I tested held up. On the dev profile, GO holds 99.6% of the activation mass, D1 0.4% and D2 exactly 0. There is zero activity in trials 0-79, and 96.2% of the mass falls in trials 90-99. 99.0% of the mass falls in the value < 5.22 bin. prev_reward==1 holds 92.8% of the mass. a2 choices hold 69.9% of the mass and S2-good steps 49% versus 31% for S1-good, so 'about 70%' is right for the a2 choice but overstates the good-state share. All test-split numbers reproduce exactly: P 0.836, R 0.809, F1 0.822, mass recall 0.921.
The claim that an unrewarded trial silences the feature mostly holds. At GO with ep_trial>=89 and prev_reward==0, the feature catches only 5.9% of the mass and has precision 0.21.

One false-positive class is systematic, not noise: the a1 / a2 asymmetry. Within the predicate, steps where the choice is a1 have precision 0.74, against 0.91 for a2. The label leaves this out; the explanation only mentions it in passing.

The misses and false positives follow the ramp. The feature builds up over consecutive rewarded GO steps, so it stays weak or silent right after a run that contained an unrewarded trial, and it keeps a decaying activation (about 0.2-0.3 of max) at GO right after an unrewarded trial. That is why recall in the lowest activation quartile is only 0.54. Requiring two rewards in a row does not fix this (test F1 0.72).

A better predicate uses only the agent's own value estimate instead of the trial counter. (phase==GO) & (value<5.22) & (prev_reward==1) scores test F1 0.860 (P 0.902, R 0.822), against 0.822 for the original. Variants with the threshold at 5.0 or 5.4 score 0.85 and 0.84. The original agent tested value < 5.22 on its own (0.76) but never value combined with prev_reward, so its framing of 'clock vs value' undersells the value version. Both predicates use only observed or agent-internal variables, and the semantics are nearly the same (low value is a correlate of the end of the episode), so this refines the label rather than refuting it.
